title: Hobbycast Episode 10: Video Podcast - Asian Cinema Nostalgia - Part 4
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rVEh3PGiggk

Part four is the Shaw Brothers episode, and it contains the series' central argument. Daniel (@dungeondive) puts *The Boxer from Shantung* at the top: his favourite martial arts film of any era, once ranked second on his all-time list behind *Once Upon a Time in the West*, a rise-and-fall gangster drama first and a fight film second. Right beside it sits *Holy Flame of the Martial World*, the most unhinged fantasy in the stack, and Daniel uses the pair to answer viewers asking why this belongs on a dungeon-crawl channel. Martial arts cinema, he argues, is the best sword and sorcery ever put on screen: lone heroes questing for magic weapons, training sequences that are literal levelling up, and a cave dungeon where the words carved on the floor come alive to attack.

The rest of the Shaw run follows: *Five Deadly Venoms* as a masked murder mystery, *The 36th Chamber of Shaolin* as a zero-to-hero training arc, *Kid with the Golden Arm* with its perfect point-A-to-point-B plot, *Kung Fu vs Yoga* and its outrageous premise, and *Chinese Super Ninjas*, the Black Belt Theater broadcast that Daniel says changed his generation the way *Star Wars* did, sending kids out to build broomstick nunchucks and origami throwing stars. Japan closes it out with *Versus* and *Zipang*, the latter recommended straight to *Shadows of Brimstone* fans.

----

Daniel calls martial arts movies the best sword and sorcery on screen. Which film would you hand a dungeon-crawl player who has never watched one?
